mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 8.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment exceeds 8.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment also rises, it may indicate inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Employment and unemployment both increase but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High CPIAUCSL indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production signals supply issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO drops below 95 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining real sales alongside high FEDFUNDS indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS and FEDFUNDS indicate slowdown but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment without corresponding S&P 500 growth may indicate other economic stresses, leading to negative returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in less than 30% of cases.
